```{r}
# helper function to label PI curve data type.
modified_DataType_piCurve <- function(df) {
  tibble(
    data_type = DataType_piCurve(data = df)$data_type,
    index_id = unique(df$index_id)
  )
}
```

## Data cleaning
```{r}
## original cleaned data from M
og_path <-  "/Users/Kathy/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UW/Desktop/UW/projects/pe_curves/mohammad/data/cleaned-data/testData/pro_hourly_growth_par-cleaned-MA-Aug6-2026.csv"

# new data I generated 
time_res <- '1H'
path <- glue(
    "/Users/Kathy/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UW/Desktop/UW/projects/",
    "pe_curves/data/clean_growth_{time_res}.csv"
  )

df_main <- read.csv(path) |>
  # change "time" col to "datetime"
  rename(datetime = time) |>
  # create new cols for year, month, and day
  mutate(
    datetime = ymd_hms(datetime),
    time = format(datetime, "%H:%M:%S"),
    yr = year(datetime),
    mnth = month(datetime),
    dy = day(datetime)
  ) |>
  # drop original index col
  select(-X) |>
  # group by each cruise, day, and population to generate integer labels for each curve
  group_by(cruise, cruise_day, pop) |>
  mutate(
    index_id = paste0("pi-", cur_group_id())
  ) |>
  ungroup() # removes grouping structure
# so far data looks good 

# print # of pi groups
cat(
    "Time resolution: ", time_res,
    " | Total PI groups: ",
    n_distinct(df_main$index_id),
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )
# Only keep the first 8 hours of each day and rename PI-model columns
max_hours = 8
df_renamed <- df_main |>
  filter(hour <= 8) |>
  # rename cols for PI curve model
  rename(
    P = slope,
    I = par_smooth
  ) |>
  mutate(
    time_res = time_res
  )
# Split data into one data frame per PI curve
df_sub <- df_renamed |>
  group_by(index_id) |>
  group_split()

# Label each PI curve, then retain time-resolution metadata.
  df_label <- parallel::mclapply(
    df_sub,
    function(x) modified_DataType_piCurve(df = x),
    mc.cores = 13
  ) |>
    bind_rows() |>
    mutate(
      time_res = time_res
    )

# count the number of data types by time resolution
df_label |>
  count(time_res, data_type) |>
  group_by(time_res) |>
  mutate(
    perc = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
  
# most datasets are uncertain and light limited for 1H data
subset(df_renamed, (cruise == 'KM1513' & pop == 'prochloro' & cruise_day == 2), select = c(I, P))
```

Helper function to upweight low irradiance values
```{r}
upweight_low_light <- function(
  df,
  irradiance_col = "I",
  low_I_min = 0,
  low_I_max = 500,
  low_I_weight = 3
) {
  # Keep all observations once.
  df_weighted <- df

  # Identify observations to replicate.
  low_I_rows <- df |>
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[irradiance_col]]),
      .data[[irradiance_col]] >= low_I_min,
      .data[[irradiance_col]] <= low_I_max
    )

  # Add extra copies. For weight = 3, each low-I observation appears 3 times total.
  if (nrow(low_I_rows) > 0 && low_I_weight > 1) {
    df_weighted <- bind_rows(
      df,
      low_I_rows[rep(seq_len(nrow(low_I_rows)), each = low_I_weight - 1), ]
    )
  }

  df_weighted
}
```

```{r}
# Lists to hold successful fit results and plot objects.
fit_par_list <- list()
weight <- 1 # set no weight for now

# run only on diel cruise now
test_diel <- subset(df_renamed, (cruise == 'KM1513' & pop == 'prochloro')) %>% arrange(cruise_day, hour)

# group by index id
df_sub <- test_diel |>
    group_by(time_res, index_id) |>
    group_split()

# loop through each PI curve and save data 
for (i in seq_along(df_sub)) {
    df <- df_sub[[i]]
    
    # Extract one value for each curve-level metadata field.
    index_id_i <- unique(df$index_id)[1]
    cruise_i <- unique(df$cruise)[1]
    cruise_day_i <- unique(df$cruise_day)[1]
    pop_i <- unique(df$pop)[1]
    
    # skip if not enough data per curve (at least 4 hours of data)
    if (nrow(df) <= 4) {
      message(
        "Skipping curve ", index_id_i,
        ": fewer than 5 rows"
      )
      next
    }
    
    # set weights for low light levels
    df_weighted <- upweight_low_light(
        df,
        irradiance_col = "I",
        low_I_min = 0,
        low_I_max = 250,
        low_I_weight = weight
    )
    
    # run weighted fit in PI model
    fit <- Fit_piModel(
        data = df_weighted,
        STATapp = "MSE"
      )
    
    # Store fitted parameter results.
      fit_par_list[[length(fit_par_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
        index_id = index_id_i,
        cruise = cruise_i,
        cruise_day = cruise_day_i,
        pop = pop_i,
        n_obs = nrow(df),
        Pmax = unname(fit$par["Pmax"]),
        alpha = unname(fit$par["alpha"]),
        beta = unname(fit$par["beta"])
      )
    # plot PI curve  
    p <- Plot_piCurve(
        fit,
        df_weighted,
        length_out = 200,
        n_cores = 6
      ) +
        ggtitle(
        paste("Day:", cruise_day_i)
        ) +
        theme(
          axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 14)
        )
    print(p + # increase the size of axis title and font
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 14)))
      
}
```



Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
